name: Harrat Khaybar
twin: Tharsis lava plains, near Arsia Mons
holds: Basalt lava flows, cinder cones and tuff rings, the same rock family that paves Tharsis
A field large enough for long rover traverses and navigation tests
Hyper-arid surface with almost no vegetation cover
breaks: The flows are thousands of years old; Tharsis lavas are hundreds of millions
Earth weathering has rounded edges and filled hollows with sand
test: Long-range rover driving and autonomous navigation across fresh basalt
plan: Long-range rover traverse with autonomous hazard avoidance across blocky basalt
Navigation without GPS using terrain-relative positioning
Suit and EVA walking trials on loose scoria

bases.task: Rover and walking traverses over boulder fields and steep slopes
Long drives across a volcanic crater floor; one of the three most-voted base zones

name: Umm Jirsan lava tube
holds: Roughly 1.5 km of passages, the longest lava tube reported in Arabia
Lunar lava tubes are leading candidates for radiation-shielded base sites
Inside, the temperature swing is far smaller than at the surface
breaks: Lunar tubes are thought to be many times wider
The cave holds air, dust and life; a lunar tube is vacuum
test: Mapping, lighting and communications inside a tube before a lunar base uses one
plan: 3D lidar mapping of a lava tube interior by a small rover or drone
Radio links from inside the tube to a surface relay
Lighting and wayfinding procedures for crews underground

bases.task: None of the nine Artemis regions has a mapped cave, so this rehearses living in a lava tube for later bases
Pits proposed as human landing candidates for shelter and buried ice

name: Harrat Rahat, 1256 CE flow
kind: Young basaltic lava flow and cones
holds: A lava flow from a historic eruption in 1256 CE, fresh and barely weathered
Chains of scoria cones along fissures, as on Elysium
Close to Madinah, so field teams can reach it in an hour
breaks: Near a city, so not an isolation analog
Seasonal plants grow between flows after rain
test: Volcanic sampling procedures and astronaut geology training
plan: Astronaut geology training on a dated (1256 CE) lava flow
Day-trip field logistics from a nearby city base

bases.task: Build landing pads and roads on flat ground before crews arrive
Make bricks and pads from basalt, the same rock family as Jezero's crater floor

name: Rub' al Khali dune sea
holds: The largest continuous sand sea on Earth
Wind shapes the same dune families that cover parts of Mars
Loose sand and dust storms to test rover wheels and filters
breaks: Light quartz sand; Martian dunes are dark basaltic sand
Dunes here move far faster in thick Earth air
test: Rover mobility in loose sand and dust-storm hardening
plan: Wheel and track mobility tests in loose sand
Dust filtration and seal testing during sandstorms
Power system tests under high dust loading

bases.task: Keep rovers moving through loose, fine soil
Proposed base zone; Opportunity was stuck in a sand ripple here for five weeks in 2005

name: Al Wahbah crater
holds: A bowl about 2 km wide and 250 m deep with steep walls
A bright salt-crusted floor, high contrast like fresh lunar craters
Steep, loose slopes to test climbing and descent
breaks: Made by a volcanic explosion, not an impact
Salt and water history that the Moon does not have
plan: Robotic descent and ascent on steep crater walls
Shadow and low-sun-angle camera tests inside a deep bowl

bases.task: Climb down and work on a crater rim in long shadows
One of the three most-voted base zones; crews reaching ground down crater walls

name: Wabar impact craters
holds: Real meteorite impact craters inside a dune sea
Impact glass and iron fragments, like ejecta at Martian craters
Craters among wind ripples, like the plains Opportunity crossed
breaks: Small craters, partly buried by moving sand
Very young impacts on a very young surface
test: Finding and sampling impact ejecta in a sand-covered plain
plan: Searching for and sampling impact ejecta and glass
Landing-site hazard mapping on a sandy plain

bases.task: Choose and certify a flat, boulder-free landing zone
Flat plains where Opportunity found an iron meteorite, like Wabar's
